scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 9b (CMO layout, alpha = 0.5), with chiplet sizes and powers from Table 2 (PDF page 5)
scenario.description: Multi-window display (MWD) system split into 12 chiplets on a passive silicon interposer. The selected scenario is the layout generated by the CMO algorithm with alpha = 0.5. The paper reports a peak temperature of 373.58 K, down from 381.41 K for the initial layout (Figure 9a). It reports communication consumption of 794.59 uJ, down from 1026.72 uJ. Layouts were verified with HotSpot 7.0 (PDF pages 3 and 10). Block coordinates appear only as grid-map figures, not numeric tables, and the packet has no linked code or data assets.
scenario.architecture: 2.5-D IC with a passive silicon interposer, 12 chiplets side by side, and a six-layer HotSpot stack. Layers from bottom to top: organic FR-4 substrate, C4 bumps, silicon interposer with TSVs, microbumps, chiplet layer, TIM. A heat spreader and fin-channel heatsink sit above the stack.
scenario.workload: Multi-window display (MWD) communication task graph of 12 IP cores (Figure 2, Table 1). Power is assumed uniform over each chiplet (Table 2).
scenario.operating_point: alpha = 0.5. Ambient 318.5 K, heat spreader edge 5 mm, heatsink edge 20 mm, forced convection with a 30 mm fin height, 1 mm fin width, 10 cm fan radius and 5000 rpm fan speed. Reported peak temperature is 373.58 K and communication consumption is 794.59 uJ.

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 7.0 (compact RC thermal model with 2.5-D/3-D support) verifies the temperature of each layout. The CMO algorithm itself is implemented in C++ (PDF pages 3 and 10).
original_setup.optimizer: Chiplet multi-objective optimization (CMO): a heuristic grid-mapping algorithm based on symmetry mapping. It combines communication-based and temperature-based heuristic information with a min-max normalised weight alpha. The selected scenario uses alpha = 0.5 (PDF pages 7-8).
original_setup.controller: None. This is a static placement study with no dynamic thermal management, DVFS or runtime controller.
original_setup.benchmark: Multi-window display (MWD) system with 12 IP cores split into 12 chiplets on a passive silicon interposer. The communication graph is in Figure 2 and Table 1, and chiplet sizes and powers are in Table 2 (PDF pages 3-5). The selected scenario is the Figure 9b layout (alpha = 0.5), reported as a CMO result against the initial layout in Figure 9a.

thermal_observable.location: Maximum (peak) system temperature of the CMO layout with alpha = 0.5 (Figure 9b), as computed by HotSpot. The text says the maximum temperature falls from 381.41 K to 373.58 K. The abstract and Section 3 also use 'average temperature' and 'peak operating temperature', so the exact chiplet or node is not stated.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Peak (maximum) temperature over the HotSpot steady-state thermal map. Averaging over the chip is not stated for this value.

physical_mismatches.reason: Cooling mismatch: the paper uses a fin-channel air-forced heatsink (30 mm fin height, 1 mm fin width, 10 cm fan radius, 5000 rpm, lateral airflow), a 5 mm spreader edge, a 20 mm heatsink edge and 318.5 K ambient. A simplified Studio package with a generic convective boundary will not reproduce this HotSpot fan and heatsink model.

Interposer stack mismatch: the paper models a six-layer stack (FR-4 organic substrate, C4 bumps, silicon interposer with TSVs, microbumps, chiplet layer, TIM) with detailed bump and TSV parameters that are not published in the packet. A simplified Studio layer stack cannot reproduce the vertical heat paths.
Solver mismatch: HotSpot's compact RC network (grid of nodes) differs from a different steady-state solver, so absolute temperatures will not match 373.58 K exactly.

Block geometry is available only as grid-map figures (Figure 9b) with theoretical sizes that include spacing. Absolute block positions are not published numerically, so the same-scenario layout cannot be reconstructed without digitising.
The CMO optimizer and its weight alpha are not reproduced by a thermal solver. They only generated the layout, so this is not a thermal mismatch if the published layout is fixed.
No controller, transient workload or reliability analysis is part of the selected scenario, so these are not mismatches. The scenario is a steady, static 2.5-D placement, not 3D stacking.

methods.note: The HotSpot 7.0 verification, the C++ CMO implementation and alpha=0.5 are supported on PDF pages 3, 8 and 10. The extraction calls the observable a 'HotSpot steady-state thermal map', but the paper never says steady-state and describes HotSpot solving transient equations with RK4. The extraction also sets experiment.kind=custom_2d_steady and steady_2d_relevant=true. The paper uses a six-layer 2.5-D stack (organic substrate, C4 bumps, interposer with TSVs, microbumps, chiplets, TIM) with a fin-channel forced-air heatsink and fan, and the extraction itself lists these as essential mismatches. Calling this a 2D reproduction is unsupported. The peak vs average temperature definition is also ambiguous, since the abstract says 'average temperature'.

code.note: No code, repository or asset is linked (assets=[], artifact_search_status checked_no_links). The pseudocode in Algorithms 1-3 is internally inconsistent. Algorithm 2 uses undefined L1/W1/k1 and loops k<L×W. Algorithm 3 tests mapflag==-2 where the text uses -1, and has malformed syntax such as D[map[i]]D[map[k]]. It hard-codes 0.186 for Ebit, which the text does not state. Eq. (1) and (2) are described as 'probability of being selected', yet the pseudocode picks the minimum cost. None of this is runnable, and the extraction does not flag it.

parameters.note: Verified on PDF page 3: ambient 318.5 K, spreader edge 5 mm, heatsink edge 20 mm, fin height 30 mm, fin width 1 mm, fan radius 10 cm, 5000 rpm. The 5 mm spreader value looks inconsistent with a 20 mm heatsink and the chiplet array, and is unresolved. The Table 2 power column is garbled in the extracted text. Only blend=5 W and mem1=10 W are read with any confidence. The other 10 chiplet powers are not extracted or verified, so the same-scenario power for every block is not established. The Ebit value, grid unit size (2 mm only inferred) and grid dimensions (Figures 3 and 4 show different column counts) are not stated.

config.note: There are no HotSpot config or floorplan files, no layer thicknesses or materials, no bump or TSV dimensions, no interposer or substrate size, and no TIM or heat-transfer coefficients. experiment.floorplan=[] and power_w={}, so no floorplan block has same-scenario power. The Figure 9b layout (alpha=0.5) was never digitised and no rendered figure image was supplied. Figure 1 dimension labels (30/20/5/1 mm) are not mapped to components.

data.note: The numbers 373.58 K, 381.41 K, 794.59 uJ and 1026.72 uJ are supported on PDF page 10, and the uJ difference 232.13 is arithmetically consistent. The paper's claimed temperature reduction of 8.34 K contradicts its own values: 381.41-373.58=7.83 K. The extraction does not flag this. The 373.58 K observable has no stated location (which chiplet or node). No decisive figure (9a-9e, 10, 2, 3) was visually verified; the supplied evidence is text only, and the block positions in Figure 9b are not obtainable.

assessment.summary: Screening label: illustrative_2d_only (the paper's 2D screening label for W4361199658, a 12-chiplet MWD 2.5-D layout from Figure 9b, CMO alpha = 0.5). Studio did NOT run: simulation status is 'skipped', simulation_allowed is false, and the experiment is custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and empty power_w, which fails input validity (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object). The illustrative verdict would normally permit a run, but the failed input gate blocks it. Because no Studio result exists and a custom 2D steady run would have no transient trace anyway, there is nothing to compare. comparison_valid is false, and the final verdict is gated to no simulation and no replication claim. The paper's reported values (peak 373.58 K for the CMO layout versus 381.41 K for the initial layout, communication consumption 794.59 uJ versus 1026.72 uJ, ambient 318.5 K) come from HotSpot 7.0 steady-state analysis with a fin-channel forced-air heatsink and a six-layer interposer stack. These cannot be numerically compared with any Studio output, since none was produced and the location, aggregation, regime, and boundary assumptions would not match. Qualitatively, the paper suggests that spreading high-power chiplets apart lowers peak temperature, which a 2D thermal model might reproduce in trend. This is only a hypothesis here; it has not been tested, and no exact replication or quantitative agreement should be claimed.
